summary: Round 2 after fix commit 5028256: all six findings resolved on disk; connect wiring is correct, fail-closed, and now proven by discriminating tests.
notes: ROUND 2 (fix commit 5028256 on ai/HEX-026). Re-ran the deterministic gate myself on the combined main...HEAD diff: contract-check ok=true, violations: none, not_checked: forbid.behaviors (evaluated by hand below). 5 files, 99 insertions / 27 deletions, within max_files_changed=5 and max_diff_lines=420; per-class: emparejamiento.go 11 (max 65), canal.go 9 (max 30), emparejamiento_test.go 83 (max 300), STATUS.md 5 (max 20). 05-validation.json round 2 records 8/8 exit 0 with go test -race clean.

FINDING 1 RESOLVED (production revert complete): canal.go:98 is back to contenedor.GetFirstDevice(ctx); grep confirms no remaining context.Background() anywhere in canal.go. The QR test now builds the session with a live context and calls cancel() AFTER NuevaSesion returns and BEFORE IniciarEmparejamientoQr, which is the correct network-free construction: GetQRChannel (qrchan.go:204-222) never inspects the context, so the failure can only come from Conectar(s.ctx). The misleading two-line comment about sqlstore ignoring the context is gone, replaced by an accurate explanation of why cancellation happens at that exact point.

FINDING 2 RESOLVED (dishonest test deleted, limitation documented honestly): TestSolicitarCodigoDeVinculacionConClienteYaConectadoNoReconecta is gone. The replacement note in emparejamiento_test.go is genuinely honest rather than a euphemism: it states that no test reaches the true branch of the !s.cliente.IsConnected() guard, that reaching it requires a real WhatsApp connection this package is forbidden to dial, and it explicitly records that the deleted test asserted the opposite of its own name by exercising the false branch. It follows the traducirItemQr sentinel pattern and cross-references TestElPayloadCentinelaDelQrNuncaLlegaAlRegistro.

FINDING 3 RESOLVED and EMPIRICALLY PROVEN: the three connect-failure tests now assert the wrapped identity ('canal: no se pudo conectar para iniciar emparejamiento QR' / '... para solicitar codigo de vinculacion'). I verified discrimination by mutation rather than by argument: in a throwaway copy of the sidecar tree outside the repo I removed both connect blocks (reconstructing the pre-fix code) and ran the package. All three FAIL against pre-fix code - the QR test on 'se esperaba un error', and the two code-pairing tests on 'error = "phone number too short"' and 'error = "international phone number required (must not start with 0)"' not containing the connect message - and all pass against the fixed code, each in 0.00s, confirming no test dials live infrastructure.

FINDING 4 RESOLVED: the honest-limitations block in emparejamiento_test.go covers all three residuals - the untestable IsConnected true branch, whatsmeow's own phone-format validation (ErrPhoneNumberTooShort / ErrPhoneNumberIsNotInternational) now unreachable because Conectar runs before PairPhone, and real QR 'code' emission - satisfying AC-3 and the forbid.behaviors bullet against fabricated green tests.

FINDING 5 RESOLVED: the two false comments in almacen_interno_test.go are corrected; the rejection is now attributed to Conectar failing on the cancelled context, not to whatsmeow inspecting the number, and the note explains what the test genuinely proves (the number never appears in the log, whatever the failure cause). Both adr-0019/adr-0010 assertions survive verbatim - EventoEmparejamientoPcSolicitado must be present, and neither '05491155551234' nor '5491155551234' may appear in the buffer - and the assertion still has content because the log line at emparejamiento.go:149 precedes the connect block. Test passes.

FINDING 6 RESOLVED: the Conectar doc comment no longer claims real-channel proof; it now states that the 2026-08-18 lab session is what FOUND the defect and that proof of this correction against the real channel remains pending - accurate. The STATUS.md bullet was moved to the end of the Definido section, immediately after HEX-025, matching the append convention of HEX-020..HEX-025; content, date (2026-08-18), HEX-026 and 'tarea 15 de la etapa A-3' trace, Spanish and vocabulary all unchanged and compliant.

AC-1 and lens-1 remain satisfied after the fix round: emparejamiento.go is byte-identical to round 1 - Conectar(s.ctx) at line 79 still precedes 'resultados := make(...)' (87) and the consumer goroutine (89), so a connect failure creates no channel and no goroutine. ConnectContext returns synchronously because NuevaSesion sets EnableAutoReconnect and InitialAutoReconnect to false (client.go:516 short-circuits the background-retry branch), so nothing relies on async reconnection.

Invariants clean: only 5 files changed, none under internal/ipc, docs/protocolo-ipc-nucleo-sidecar.md, sidecar/go.mod or sidecar/go.sum; 11 IPC message types and wire version 4 intact, whatsmeow pin unchanged, no new dependency, no Rust file touched. manejo.go untouched, so the phone number still comes only from configuration.

ACCEPTED RESIDUALS carried to the human gate (all documented in code, none blocking): (a) the IsConnected true branch of SolicitarCodigoDeVinculacion has no unit coverage and cannot have any without a live channel; (b) this correction has not yet been exercised against real WhatsApp infrastructure - the lab session of plan task 15 must be re-run to confirm the QR actually appears, which is precisely what the human gate is for; (c) whatsmeow's internal QR-channel event handler registered by GetQRChannel is not removable on a synchronous connect failure with the pinned API, a bounded per-attempt residual already recorded as a blueprint risk.
